blocks.x: Neuromorphic & Emerging Compute Advisory as delivered by Dataq Software: scope, delivery pattern, the platforms involved and the outcomes we commit to at each gate.

The advanced-compute landscape keeps birthing new silicon: neuromorphic chips for event-driven sensing, photonic accelerators for inference, in-memory compute for energy-bound workloads, domain-specific ASICs for inference economics. We run a standing advisory that tracks these with technology-readiness scoring, vendor due diligence, and workload-fit analysis — so when a technology crosses your relevance threshold, you move in weeks with a designed pilot, not months from a cold start.

The advisory includes an annual technology review with kill-or-continue decisions, pilot governance identical to our quantum discipline (classical baselines, pre-agreed criteria), and a watchlist tied to your workload roadmap. It is deliberately a small retainer: the value is preparedness, not perpetual consulting.

Delivery follows the same weekly rhythm on every program of this type. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
